title: Insulating the floor of a ground-floor bay window
subtitle: Stopping cold coming up through the bay window floor projection
excerpt: The projecting floor of a Victorian bay window is one of the coldest spots in a typical terrace. Three sides of the bay floor cantilever out over cold external air, and the floor is usually uninsulated. Fitting insulation boards into the bay floor soffit cuts the cold significantly.
sourceNotes: STBA (Sustainable Traditional Buildings Alliance) guidance on bay windows and thermal bypass; English Heritage energy efficiency in traditional buildings (2011); BRE BR 262 thermal bridging examples for bay windows.

glossaryTerms.definition: A path through a building element that conducts heat more readily than the surrounding insulation, causing localised cold spots and condensation risk.
Polyisocyanurate rigid insulation board, a closed-cell foam product with high thermal resistance per mm, commonly used in floor, wall, and roof insulation.

projectSchedule.title: Measure and cut boards
projectSchedule.body: Measure the bay soffit panel openings accurately and cut the PIR boards to fit. Leave a 3 mm gap around each board for the adhesive foam.

projectSchedule.title: Fit boards and fill edges
projectSchedule.body: Bond boards in place with low-expansion PU foam. Fill the perimeter gap with fire-rated intumescent foam where the board meets the structural beam.

projectSchedule.title: Check for cold spots
projectSchedule.body: After one cold night, walk barefoot across the bay area. If the floor still feels noticeably cold, check that the board edges are sealed and that there is no gap at the junction with the main floor.

content.text: The projecting floor of a Victorian bay window is a cantilever slab. It sits between the front wall and the main ground floor. Three faces of the bay floor expose the underside to cold external air.
A
thermal bridge

runs around the perimeter where the bay frame meets the main wall. Fitting insulation boards across the soffit of the bay and sealing the perimeter junction cuts the cold floor and reduces heating demand in the bay area.
What you'll need
Materials
50 mm PIR board, enough to cover the bay soffit panels (typical bay soffit: 0.5 to 1.2 m²)
Low-expansion polyurethane adhesive foam for bonding the boards to the soffit deck
Intumescent fire-rated foam to seal the perimeter gaps where the board meets the structural timber
Aluminium tape for sealing board-to-board joints
Tools
Tape measure, pencil
Straight edge and craft knife (or a fine-toothed saw) for cutting PIR cleanly
Access ladder to reach the bay soffit (typically 600 to 800 mm above ground)
Before you start cutting or drilling. Eye protection for every cut. Wear gloves when handling cut PIR board, the edges are sharp. Keep a dust mask handy; PIR offcuts produce fine foam dust when sawn.
The installation
Measure each soffit panel opening precisely. Bay soffits on terraced houses are often slightly out of square; measure both diagonals.
Cut the
PIR board
to fit each opening with a 3 to 5 mm clearance around the perimeter. A tight fit without adhesive risks the board falling out as the adhesive foam sets.

Apply low-expansion PU adhesive foam in a perimeter bead and two diagonal lines across the board face. Press the board up into the soffit opening and hold for 60 seconds while the foam begins to grip.

Fill the perimeter gap between the board edge and the timber frame with intumescent fire-rated foam. Standard low-expansion foam is not fire-rated. Use fire-rated foam wherever insulation sits next to a structural timber member.
Tape all board-to-board joints with aluminium tape. This closes the small gaps at board edges that are otherwise the weakest thermal paths.
Check the junction where the bay meets the main ground-floor structure. The gap between the bay soffit boards and the main floor zone is the remaining thermal bridge; seal it with low-expansion foam.
What to expect

After one heating season the bay floor temperature typically rises by 3 to 6°C under cold conditions. This is especially noticeable if the bay is used as a sitting area. The junction with the main wall will remain slightly cooler than the central bay floor; that residual cold bridge is reduced but not eliminated by this approach.

rows.symptom: Board falls out of soffit opening within a week
rows.cause: PU foam under-applied or board cut too large creating stress on the glue bond
rows.fix: Remove board; clean off old foam; re-cut with 5 mm clearance; apply foam in a continuous perimeter bead plus two diagonal runs; hold in place for 2 minutes while foam cures.

rows.symptom: Cold draught felt around the edge of the bay soffit inside the room
rows.cause: Gap at the junction between the bay soffit insulation and the main floor structure
rows.fix: Seal the perimeter gap from below with low-expansion foam and cover with a plaster coving or quadrant bead.
